To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Internet is being driven towards a future of corporate control, security, and sustainability, and that these drivers are shaping the Internet’s development in ways that will make it a less democratic and more commercialized space.

the Internet is a complex and dynamic social, technical and economic system, which is being transformed by the interplay between its technical and economic drivers and the political, social and environmental forces that shape them.

the future of the Internet will be shaped by corporate, security, and ecological drivers, which will lead to a monopolization of Internet governance and the construction of the Internet as a commercialized, securitized, or environmentalized space.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how Internet futures are being shaped by the interests of the Internet’s corporate stakeholders, and what the implications of those futures are.
the question of how we can understand the future of the Internet and its governance, in the light of the fact that it is already in a state of flux, and that its governance is changing as well.
the ways in which the Internet is being shaped by the interests and values of its most influential actors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Internet has always been shaped by its users, and will continue to be so.
the Internet is a complex system that has evolved over time, with different actors and forces influencing its development.

the Internet’s future is being shaped by a complex and dynamic interplay of forces and trends that will likely lead to a future that is both centralized and securitized, with corporate and governmental interests dominating the Internet’s governance and architecture, and with the Internet becoming increasingly surveilled as it becomes an increasingly scarce resource.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this chapter argues that the future of the Internet will be shaped by corporate interests, cybersecurity concerns, and environmental change.

this chapter argues for the need to understand how the Internet is being shaped by the forces that drive it, especially economics, security, environmental change, and governance, and how the Internet is shaping the future of our world.
the Internet is a space that is increasingly being shaped by economic interests and that these interests are shaping the Internet in a way that is not necessarily in the public good.

the Internet is being governed by a combination of these drivers and that the Internet will continue to be a site of contestation between these forces and their respective futures.
the Internet’s development is being driven by the interests of powerful economic and political actors, and that the Internet’s future is being shaped by the interests of these same groups.
the future of cyberspace is being shaped in ways that are not necessarily democratic or open to public input.
